lesson.opening: Why did a shared Greek culture coexist with many separate political communities?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
Polis and citizenship

Colonization and sea routes

Athens and Sparta as distinct institutions

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: Shared language and religious festivals did not create a single state. Compare institutions, geography, and economic arrangements rather than explaining everything through national character.

sections.heading: Keep the question
sections.body: Why did a shared Greek culture coexist with many separate political communities?

activities.prompt: Which happened first: “Expansion of Greek settlement overseas” or “Cleisthenes’ reforms”?
activities.hint: Compare the dates on the unit timeline.

activities.prompt: “Mountainous terrain made political unification impossible.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: Geography helps explain opportunities and obstacles; “impossible” is a causal conclusion contradicted by later political combinations.

activities.prompt: Put these events back in chronological order.
Explain what a polis is, including who participates and who does not.
activities.instructions: A few sentences are enough. Cite a passage when it helps.
